from.place: Proof paragraph 2, middle derived mapping-complex comparison before the inverse limit: Infinity-categorical monadicity and the augmented counit bar resolution.

title: Infinity-categorical monadicity and the augmented counit bar resolution
statement:
Use coherent diagrams, mapping spaces, equivalences and limiting or colimiting cocones as defined in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. In particular, coherent diagrams are simplicial maps into quasicategories, transformations are edges of the internal functor simplicial set, and colimiting cocones are initial objects of the coherent comma cocone category, using its right-pinched mapping spaces and weak contractibility. A diagram indexed by an ordinary category $J$ means a diagram on its nerve $N(J)$. Use infinity categories modeled by simplicial sets [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set] with fillers for all inner horns; an inner horn is the union of all faces of a standard simplex except one face other than its first and last. Work in universes large enough for the categories and simplicial diagrams below. Let $L:\mathcal C\rightleftarrows\mathcal D:U$ be an adjunction of infinity categories, with unit $\eta$ and counit $\epsilon$. Its monad is $T=UL$, with multiplication $U\epsilon L$ and unit $\eta$. An algebra for $T$ is a left module for this associative algebra in the category of endofunctors of $\mathcal C$ under composition: its data are an object $A$, an action $TA\to A$, and unital associative action homotopies and all higher compatibilities. Write $\operatorname{Alg}_T(\mathcal C)$ for the infinity category retaining all coherent transformations between these actions. A geometric realization here is the infinity-categorical colimit of a simplicial diagram indexed by $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$, where $\Delta$ is the category of finite nonempty ordered sets and order-preserving maps.

Assume $\mathcal D$ admits geometric realizations, $U$ preserves them, and $U$ is conservative, meaning a morphism in $\mathcal D$ is an equivalence whenever its image under $U$ is. Then the comparison
$$\mathcal D\longrightarrow\operatorname{Alg}_T(\mathcal C),\qquad Z\longmapsto(UZ,U\epsilon_Z)$$
is an equivalence over $\mathcal C$, including mapping spaces and coherent composition. For every $Z\in\mathcal D$, the augmented simplicial bar object
$$B_r Z=L(UL)^r UZ\quad(r\geq0),\qquad B_\bullet Z\longrightarrow Z$$
has geometric realization $Z$, naturally in $Z$. Its faces apply the counit at each possible adjacent $LU$, its degeneracies insert $L\eta U$, and its augmentation is the counit. After applying $U$ the augmentation is split by the extra degeneracy inserting $\eta$ before the first factor. All these structures are coherent diagrams of the given adjunction, rather than formulas only in its ordinary homotopy category.

source.place: General monadic/bar foundation for paragraph 2; WANTED: Lurie, Higher Algebra (2017), Theorem 4.7.3.5, Lemma 4.7.3.13 and its proof, Proposition 4.7.3.14 and Remark 4.7.3.15; Example 4.7.2.7 supplies the split augmented bar. Read online https://people.math.harvard.edu/~lurie/papers/HA.pdf, printed pp. 685-689; not archived. No Stacks tag gives infinity-categorical Barr--Beck or its coherent bar realization.

external.place: Higher Algebra (2017), Theorem 4.7.3.5(c), Lemma 4.7.3.13 and its proof, Proposition 4.7.3.14 and Remark 4.7.3.15, printed pp. 685-689; Example 4.7.2.7 for the split augmented bar.

proof.text: Put $\mathcal A=\operatorname{Alg}_T(\mathcal C)$, and write $V:\mathcal A\to\mathcal C$ and $F:\mathcal C\to\mathcal A$ for the forgetful and free adjunction in [lem-coef-infinity-free-module-bar]. Write $K:\mathcal D\to\mathcal A$ for the comparison in the statement, so $VK=U$ with its specified coherence. At $c\in\mathcal C$, $KLc$ is $ULc=Tc$ with action $U\epsilon_{Lc}=\mu_c$, including the same coherent action data as the free module $Fc$. Thus $KL\simeq F$. For every $Z$ the original adjunction and the free adjunction give $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal D}(Lc,Z)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(c,UZ)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal A}(Fc,KZ)$. This is the actual comparison-induced map: a map $f:Lc\to Z$ goes under the free adjunction to $U(f)\eta_c$, its original adjunct. In particular the universal arrow $Fc\to K(Lc)$ has underlying map $1_{Tc}$, since $\mu_c T\eta_c=1_{Tc}$.

source.place: Lemma 4.7.3.13, proof: free objects belong to the domain of the partial left adjoint; online, not archived.

proof.text: Let $\mathcal A_0$ be the full subcategory on objects equivalent to some $Fc$. Step 1 supplies universal arrows $M\to K(GM)$ with $GM=Lc$ when $M=Fc$. Existence for an equivalent free object follows by precomposing the universal arrow by its specified equivalence. Apply the opposite assertion of [lem-coef-parametric-universal-arrows] to obtain a coherent partial left adjoint $G:\mathcal A_0\to\mathcal D$ and coherent universal transformation $u:\iota\to KG$. Its components are equivalences: on $Fc$ this is the identity on the free action from Step 1, and any other universal-arrow choice is equivalent by the contractibility assertion of the same node. The functor-category component criterion makes $u$ a coherent natural equivalence. Hence $UG\simeq V\iota$ coherently, and all morphisms between free objects, including those not induced by a map of their generators, have been lifted by this partial adjoint.

source.place: Lemma 4.7.3.13, proof: the partial left adjoint on the full subcategory of corepresentable modules; online, not archived.

proof.text:
For $M=(A,a)$ take the coherent free resolution $R_\bullet M\to M$ of [lem-coef-infinity-free-module-bar]. Its entire simplicial diagram factors through the full subcategory $\mathcal A_0$, because all vertices are free modules; fullness retains every simplex. Define $P_\bullet(M)=G(R_\bullet M)$ and $H(M)=|P_\bullet(M)|$ in $\mathcal D$. This realization exists by the hypothesis on $\mathcal D$; no realization of an arbitrary diagram in $\mathcal C$ or $\mathcal A$ is asserted. The mapping-space colimit criterion, the coherent partial adjunction, and the colimit assertion for $R_\bullet M$ give, naturally in $Z$,
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal D}(H(M),Z)\simeq\lim_{[r]\in\Delta}\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal D}(P_r(M),Z)\simeq\lim_{[r]\in\Delta}\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal A}(R_rM,KZ)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal A}(M,KZ).$$
The middle equivalence respects the whole cosimplicial diagram by the coherent partial adjunction, not just its vertices. Explicitly, by the dual cocone clause of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] the outer two equivalences are $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal D}(H(M),Z)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(N(\Delta)^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal D)}(P_\bullet(M),\Delta Z)$ and $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal A}(M,KZ)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(N(\Delta)^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal A)}(R_\bullet M,\Delta KZ)$, and the dual functor-category formula of [lem-coef-parametric-universal-arrows], applied with $B=R_\bullet M$ and the constant diagram at $Z$ (whose image under $K$ is the constant diagram at $KZ$), identifies these two mapping spaces. Apply the dual pointwise adjoint criterion to these representing objects to obtain $H\dashv K$ with coherent unit $\alpha$ and counit $\beta$.

source.place: Lemma 4.7.3.13, proof: corepresent the mapping functor by the realization of the lifted free resolution; online, not archived.

proof.text:
The unit $\alpha_M:M\to KH(M)$ is the map induced from the coherent cocone $R_rM\xrightarrow{u}KP_r(M)\to KH(M)$. Indeed this cocone is the image of $1_{H(M)}$ under the displayed representing equivalence of Step 3; this identifies the unit rather than merely some map with the same source and target. Since $VR_\bullet M\to A$ is split, [lem-coef-infinity-split-augmentation-colimit] identifies its realization with $A$. The coherent equivalence $u$ of Step 2 identifies this diagram with $UP_\bullet(M)$. Consequently the underlying unit is the composite
$$A\simeq|VR_\bullet M|\xrightarrow{|Vu|}|UP_\bullet(M)|\longrightarrow U|P_\bullet(M)|=UH(M).$$
The last arrow is the canonical colimit comparison, an equivalence by preservation of realizations by $U$. Thus $V\alpha_M$ is an equivalence. Conservativity of $V$, supplied by the free-module lemma, makes $\alpha_M$ an equivalence in $\mathcal A$.

source.place: Lemma 4.7.3.13, proof: underlying comparison unit is the realization comparison map; online, not archived.

proof.text: For $Z\in\mathcal D$, the triangle identity $K(\beta_Z)\alpha_{KZ}\simeq1_{KZ}$ and Step 4 imply that $K(\beta_Z)$ is an equivalence. Applying $V$ shows that $U(\beta_Z)$ is an equivalence, and the assumed conservativity of $U$ makes $\beta_Z$ an equivalence. The component criterion upgrades $\alpha$ and $\beta$ to coherent natural equivalences. Thus $H$ and $K$ are coherent quasi-inverses. This is an equivalence over $\mathcal C$: the comparison already satisfies $VK\simeq U$, and $V\alpha:V\simeq UH$ supplies the compatibility for its inverse. The mapping-space clause follows from the functor-equivalence assertion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus]; composition is respected by the coherent functors and these coherent equivalence witnesses.

source.place: Theorem 4.7.3.5, proof after Lemma 4.7.3.13: conservative comparison with fully faithful left adjoint; online, not archived.

proof.text: We identify the lifted resolution at $M=KZ$ explicitly. Its terms are $P_r(KZ)=G(F(T^rUZ))\simeq L T^rUZ$. The degree-zero augmentation, adjunct to the action of $KZ$, is $\epsilon_Z:LUZ\to Z$. For $r\geq1$ the first face of the free resolution is the free-module counit, whose image under $G$ is $\epsilon_{L T^{r-1}UZ}:LUL T^{r-1}UZ\to L T^{r-1}UZ$: its adjunct is the identity on $T^rUZ$, by the triangle identity. For $1\leq i<r$, the $i$th face is $L T^{i-1}(\mu_{T^{r-i-1}UZ})$, while the last is $L T^{r-1}(U\epsilon_Z)$. Substituting $\mu=U\epsilon L$ shows that these are exactly the counit applied at the $r+1$ possible $LU$ positions in $(LU)^{r+1}Z$. For $0\leq i\leq r$ the degeneracy is $L T^i(\eta_{T^{r-i}UZ})$, inserting $L\eta U$ between the corresponding adjacent $LU$ factors. These identifications hold coherently: the formulas are the mates of the specified free-module operators under the coherent partial adjunction, whose functor-category version in [lem-coef-parametric-universal-arrows] retains all simplices and commutes with restriction. Hence this is the actual augmented counit bar $B_\bullet Z$, natural in $Z$, and not a diagram built only in the homotopy category.

source.place: Proof of Lemma 4.7.3.13, Proposition 4.7.3.14 and Remark 4.7.3.15: identify the lifted free bar for a comparison algebra; online, not archived.

proof.text: Applying $U$ to Step 6 gives exactly the underlying module bar $VR_\bullet(KZ)\to UZ$. Its coherent splitting, supplied by [lem-coef-infinity-free-module-bar], has $h_{-1}=\eta_{UZ}$ and $h_r=\eta_{T^{r+1}UZ}$, so inserts the unit before the first factor. By [lem-coef-infinity-split-augmentation-colimit] this augmentation is colimiting. If $b_Z:|B_\bullet Z|\to Z$ is the map induced by its augmentation, the composite $|UB_\bullet Z|\to U|B_\bullet Z|\xrightarrow{U b_Z}UZ$ is the equivalence given by that split augmentation. The first map is an equivalence by the preservation hypothesis, so $U b_Z$, and then $b_Z$ by conservativity, is an equivalence. Thus the specified augmented bar realizes $Z$. Naturality includes the augmentation and the splitting, since the module bar, partial adjunction and realization all used coherent functors. The same mapping-space criterion used in Step 3 makes the space of colimiting choices contractible, so no unrelated objectwise choices replace this coherent construction.

source.place: Example 4.7.2.7 and Proposition 4.7.3.14 with Remark 4.7.3.15: split counit bar and its natural augmentation; online, not archived.
